title: All the dangerous products pulled from Aussie shelves this week - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia
text:
Product recall roundup: Bunnings and Big W kitchen item, BCF camping tent, torch keychain, hoodie - Yahoo Lifestyle Australia Search query for Search the web Search the web Skip to main 
 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Product recall roundup: Bunnings and Big W kitchen item, BCF camping tent, torch keychain, hoodie
 Refunds are available for Aussies who return the items, but some brands have asked for proof of purchase. 
 Stewart Perrie Sat 14 November 2026 at 6:00 pm UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Items available across the country have been recalled this week after critical issues were discovered.
 Some were sold at big-name retailers like Bunnings and BCF , while others were sold in just one state.
 Yahoo Lifestyle has done a wrap-up of the items to be aware of.
 Items sold at big-name retailers like Bunnings and BCF have been recalled this week.
 (Getty/Samuel Wiki (Creative Commons)) Darche's Solar Roof Top Tent was recalled due to a manufacturing issue that could increase the risk of death.
 It was sold at stores such as BCF , Roof Racks Galor, Mudgee Camoing & 4WD, and Tentworld between July 2025 and November this year.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The product's hinges can fail, causing the roof to separate from the rest of the tent when mounted on the vehicle.
 The Darche Solar Roof Top Tent was sold at places such as BCF, Roof Racks Galore, Tentworld, Lyal Eales Stores and Opposite Lock Kununurra.
 (Australian Competition and Consumer Commission) "Risk of death, serious injury or property damage (including to other road users) if the tent's roof separates from the tent when mounted to the vehicle," the recall from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission stated.
 "Incidents of the hinges cracking have occurred."
 Australians have been instructed to immediately stop driving with the impacted product mounted to their car.
 "Contact Darche to arrange for a refund, replacement product or a technician to replace the hinges free of charge," the recall added.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement You can contact the company on 1300 367 695 from 9am to 5pm, Monday to Friday or email them at recall@darche.com.au .

 Common kitchen appliance that could break
 A kettle sold at Big W, Bunnings, Amazon, and other retailers was pulled from shelves as it could break "without any warning".
 Ozdingo issued an alert on Friday for its Kitchee 1.7L cordless glass electric kettle.
 The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) website said the kettle posed a risk of serious burns or scalding from hot water if it breaks, as well as cuts and lacerations from broken glass.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The product was available for sale nationally from May 2022 until October this year.
 Customers are urged to stop using the kettle immediately and unplug it from the power supply.
 (ACCC) To identify the product, check if it has the following identifying numbers, which can be located on the bottom of the kettle or on the box:
 Model numbers: FY788 or FY999
 PRA number: 2026/21110
 It was also sold at Dick Smith, eBay, Kogan, MyDeal, Woolworths Everyday Market, and Dropshipzone.
 Customers are urged to stop using the kettle and unplug it from the power supply.
 Send a clear photo of the affected kettle to Ozdingo or to the place where you purchased it, showing the product and model number. You'll also have to provide your order details as proof of purchase to receive a full refund.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Contact Ozdingo via email (helpdesk@ozdingo.com.au) or visit the website for further assistance.
 Children's hoodie that doesn't comply with major standards
 Reddot Home issued an alert about its Kids Cuddle Hoodies because they don't comply with the mandatory standard for children's nightwear.
 The fire hazard warning label is sewn into the product's side seam rather than at the required neck position.
 This hoodie and others have been recalled over an issue with warning labels.
 (ACCC) There is a risk of "serious burn injuries" if the product is exposed to a heat source or flame and ignites, and "consumers may not be aware of this risk".
 The garments were available for sale from April to September this year in Western Australia and affected batches will have the SKU number of 753068.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement You can contact the company for a full refund by emailing recalls@reddot.com.au . 
 Keychain with crucial error on button batteries
 History & Heraldry (Australia) Pty Ltd recalled its Super Torch keychain as its button battery compartment is not adequately secured, and the button batteries are accessible.
 The item is also missing warning information about the dangers of button batteries to children and what to do if someone suspects they have swallowed or placed a button battery inside any part of their body.
 Affected product codes range from 877000001 to 877000492, and the issue applies to four different product colours.
 The keyring torch didn't have crucial information about button batteries.
 (ACCC) They've been available for sale around the country since 2021, were only pulled in October 12.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Stop using the product immediately and keep the batteries out of reach of children," the ACCC alert said.
 You can return the product to the place of purchase for a full refund.
 If you need more information, you can contact History & Heraldry Australia Pty Ltd on 08 9455 1615. '
